summary:
Farmer Query · Agricultural Explorer is an interactive web platform designed to empower farmers, agronomists, and researchers with actionable climate and soil intelligence for crop selection. By leveraging real-time spatial APIs from NASA POWER (temporal daily and climatology parameters such as T2M, PRECTOTCORR, RH2M, and WS10M), Open-Meteo DEM elevation data, and ISRIC SoilGrids, the application processes local agroecological conditions dynamically.

The core engine combines FAO EcoCrop-style trapezoidal suitability models, weighted geometric scoring (incorporating Liebig's Law of the Minimum), and an automated 9-scenario sensitivity analysis (+-1 °C, +-15% rainfall) to evaluate crop viability and yield stability under climate variability. It provides interactive heatmaps for temperature, precipitation, wind, altitude, and soil clay/pH, rendering clear scorecards, verdict classifications, and primary limiting factors. This tool addresses agricultural climate vulnerability, helping smallholders make data-driven planting decisions, minimize crop failure, and optimize soil resilience.
details:
1. 1. What does it do & How does it work?

Farmer Query · Agricultural Explorer is a web application designed to bridge the gap between complex satellite Earth observation data and practical farm decision-making.

When a user selects any geographical coordinate via the interactive globe, a Leaflet map interface or location search:

  • Data Acquisition: The application concurrently queries the NASA POWER API (daily and climatology endpoints for 2-meter air temperature, total corrected precipitation, relative humidity, and 10-meter wind speed), Open-Meteo DEM API for precise elevation data, and ISRIC SoilGrids WMS/REST API for surface soil pH and clay content.
  • Agroecological Engine (FAO EcoCrop Model): The system evaluates 13 key crops (Maize, Beans, Arabica Coffee, Rice, Sugarcane, Tomato, Potato, Wheat, Cassava, Banana, Cocoa, Sorghum, Soybean) against custom multi-dimensional trapezoidal membership functions.
    • Show crop regions animates the 3D globe stop by stop (up to 15 regions), with an information card for each region (crop, location, coordinates, average annual temperature and rainfall).
    • Go to best match flies the globe straight to the closest region. If nothing falls within the chosen tolerance, the 5 closest regions are shown instead.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Reduces Crop Failure: Helps farmers identify whether a specific crop is marginal or non-viable before investing capital in planting.
  • Climate Resilience: Sensitivity variance indicators inform growers about how vulnerable a crop is to seasonal climate shifts.
  • Accessibility: Converts raw NASA satellite and reanalysis data into intuitive star ratings, percentage scores, and plain-language agronomic advice.
  • Faster discovery: Growers can ask “where does this crop thrive?” and compare their own land with the world’s leading production regions, instead of testing locations one by one.
  • Intuitive exploration: One shared 3D globe, with an interactive panel and animated tours, makes climate and crop concepts easy to grasp for non-technical users.

3. Tools, Languages, Frameworks & APIs Used

  • Frontend Framework: Next.js (App Router), React, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS Modules / Tailwind.
  • Mapping & Geospatial: Leaflet.js, OpenStreetMap tiles, ISRIC SoilGrids WMS layer, custom Canvas/SVG heatmaps. three.js for the interactive 3D globe.
  • Data & APIs: NASA POWER API (/api/temporal/daily/point, /api/temporal/climatology/point, /api/temporal/daily/regional), Open-Meteo Elevation API, ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 REST API, Nominatim OpenStreetMap Geocoding.
  • Algorithms: Multi-scenario climate sensitivity analysis, trapezoidal agroecological scoring, weighted geometric mean, Liebig’s Law of the Minimum engine. Distance-based matching in normalized temperature–rainfall space with an adjustable tolerance.
  • UI & animation: Reusable React components (parameter panel, globe decoration), SVG and CSS animations that respect reduced-motion preferences.

4. Creativity & Key Considerations

Unlike static recommendation tables, Farmer Query implements a dynamic multi-scenario stress tester directly in the client runtime. It accounts for soil-climate interactions, handles missing spatial data gracefully with contextual fallbacks, and presents complex atmospheric data through interactive spatial visualizations. It also works in both directions: from a place to the crops that suit it, and from a crop’s conditions to the places in the world that match them, all explored on a single animated globe.
